subject: anatomy
title: Peritoneal Spaces: Morison Pouch, Pelvic Pouches, and Gutters

steps.tx: The complex embryological rotations of the gut divide the peritoneal cavity into interconnecting recesses and gutters. The **Morison pouch** (hepatorenal recess) is the lowest gravity-dependent space of the upper peritoneal cavity in a supine patient, situated between the visceral surface of the right hepatic lobe and the anterior surface of the right kidney.
steps.say: Gut rotations divide the peritoneal cavity into interconnected recesses and gutters. Morison pouch between the liver and right kidney is the lowest space in a supine patient, collecting dependent fluid.

vis.alt: Abdominal radiograph showing gas patterns and peritoneal anatomical recesses
vis.caption: Radiographic anatomy of abdominal recesses and potential peritoneal fluid reservoirs. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In the erect posture, the lowest point of the entire peritoneal cavity in females is the **rectouterine pouch** of Douglas, situated between the posterior wall of the uterus and the anterior wall of the rectum. In males, the corresponding dependent pelvic space is the rectovesical pouch between rectum and urinary bladder.
steps.say: In the standing female, the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity is the rectouterine pouch of Douglas. In males, the corresponding dependent pelvic pocket is the rectovesical pouch.

left.title: Female: Pouch of Douglas
points: Separated from posterior vaginal fornix by 1.5 cm
Accessible to culdocentesis through posterior fornix
Common site for pelvic abscess or endometriosis

right.title: Male: Rectovesical Pouch
points: Lies 7.5 cm from the anal verge
Accumulates infected exudate or malignant deposits

steps.tx: Aspiration of fluid from the rectouterine pouch via the posterior vaginal fornix is termed **culdocentesis**. A needle advanced through the posterior fornix directly punctures the pouch of Douglas: non-clotting blood confirms ruptured ectopic pregnancy, purulent fluid confirms pelvic inflammatory disease, and malignant ascites confirms ovarian carcinomatosis.
steps.say: Aspiration of the rectouterine pouch through the posterior vaginal fornix is called culdocentesis. Obtaining non-clotting blood confirms a ruptured ectopic pregnancy, while pus indicates pelvic peritonitis.

nodes.label: Needle Puncture Through Posterior Vaginal Fornix
Non-clotting Dark Blood: Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy
Turbid Purulent Exudate: Pelvic Abscess / Tubo-ovarian Sepsis
Dry Tap: Inconclusive; Mandates Diagnostic Laparoscopy

steps.tx: The small intestine is anchored to the posterior abdominal wall by the **mesentery** (mesentery proper), a fan-shaped double peritoneal fold. Its root measures fifteen centimetres in length, extending obliquely downwards and to the right from the duodenojejunal flexure (L2) to the upper border of the right sacroiliac joint.
steps.say: The small intestine is suspended by the fan-shaped mesentery. Its root spans fifteen centimeters obliquely from the duodenojejunal flexure at L2 to the right sacroiliac joint.

rows: Oblique line from L2 to right SI joint
Apex at bifurcation of left common iliac
Sigmoid vessels and superior rectal artery

steps.tx: Lateral to the ascending and descending colons lie the longitudinal **paracolic gutters**. The right paracolic gutter is deeper and continuous superiorly with the hepatorenal pouch and subphrenic spaces, while the left paracolic gutter is separated from the left subphrenic space by the phrenicocolic ligament (sustentaculum lienis).
steps.say: Lateral to the colons lie the paracolic gutters. The right gutter communicates freely with the hepatorenal space, while the left is blocked from the spleen by the phrenicocolic ligament.

left.title: Right Paracolic Gutter
points: Wider and deeper than left gutter
Direct conduit from appendix to Morison pouch
Transmits appendiceal pus upward to subphrenic space

right.title: Left Paracolic Gutter
points: Narrower and shallower than right gutter
Prevents pelvic infection from reaching spleen
Conveys fluid primarily downward toward pelvis

steps.tx: The spaces between the diaphragm and the superior surface of the liver are the **subphrenic spaces**, partitioned into right and left spaces by the falciform ligament. Subphrenic abscesses typically develop following gastric or duodenal ulcer perforation, presenting with high spiking fevers, right shoulder tip pain, and diaphragmatic immobility.
steps.say: The subphrenic spaces lie between the diaphragm and liver, divided by the falciform ligament. Subphrenic abscesses follow perforated ulcers, presenting with fever and referred shoulder pain.

vis.alt: Peritoneal reflections and compartments illustrating subphrenic and paracolic anatomy
vis.caption: Anatomy of the subphrenic spaces and peritoneal compartmentalization of peritonitis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Organs covered only on their anterior surfaces by parietal peritoneum are classified as **retroperitoneal organs**. Easily remembered by the mnemonic SAD PUCKER, these comprise: Suprarenal glands, Aorta/IVC, Duodenum (second and third parts), Pancreas (except tail), Ureters, Colon (ascending and descending), Kidneys, Esophagus, and Rectum.
steps.say: Organs covered only anteriorly by peritoneum are retroperitoneal, recalled by the mnemonic SAD PUCKER: suprarenals, aorta, duodenum, pancreas, ureters, colon, kidneys, esophagus, and rectum.

rows: Capped above kidneys in Gerota fascia
Head, neck, and body (tail is intraperitoneal)
Traversed by splenic vessels in retroperitoneum
Cross common or external iliac bifurcation

steps.tx: Retroperitoneal organ injuries produce insidious clinical signs because extravasated blood and digestive enzymes are sequestered behind the peritoneum, delaying overt signs of **peritonitis**. Traumatic duodenal or pancreatic ruptures initially cause back pain rather than acute anterior guarding, demanding urgent contrast-enhanced CT scanning.
steps.say: Retroperitoneal injuries produce subtle early signs because extravasated fluid is trapped behind the peritoneum. Pancreatic or duodenal rupture causes back pain rather than anterior guarding.

nodes.label: Blunt Compression Trauma (Handlebar or Seatbelt Impact)
Retroperitoneal Rupture of Duodenum or Pancreatic Neck
Absence of Acute Anterior Abdominal Peritonism
Immediate Contrast-enhanced CT Identifies Retroperitoneal Gas
